summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 has consolidated around the major hyperscalers — AWS, Azure, and Google — each offering managed access to foundation models within the customer's own cloud security perimeter, with no single 'winner' but rather a best fit based on existing cloud footprint and model preferences. Beyond the big three, data-platform-native options like Snowflake Cortex and Databricks bring AI to where enterprise data already lives, while IBM watsonx targets governance-heavy regulated industries and Cloudflare Workers AI serves edge/low-latency inference. The key decision drivers are existing cloud contracts, required model diversity, data residency, and compliance posture rather than raw model quality.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy — prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay within the enterprise's own cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train the provider's models, unlike sending data to a consumer-grade vendor API.

Compliance and certifications — aggregators inherit the cloud's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR, and regional controls, making audits and regulatory sign-off dramatically easier than a standalone model vendor.

Consolidated billing and existing contracts — AI spend flows through the same cloud enterprise agreement, committed-use discounts, and procurement relationship already in place, avoiding new vendor onboarding.

Model choice behind one API — a single managed endpoint provides access to Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, and others, letting teams switch or multi-source models without re-architecting integrations.
Enterprise security and operations — native VPC isolation, private networking, IAM/RBAC, audit logging, encryption with customer-managed keys, and observability tooling that consumer APIs lack.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry)
available_models: Models-as-a-Service catalog (Llama, Mistral, Cohere, others via Azure AI Foundry)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; discounts via Azure Enterprise Agreement.
key_features: Content filtering & Azure AI Content Safety
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises wanting the latest OpenAI models with enterprise governance inside Azure.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing, Batch (discounted), and Provisioned Throughput (model units) for reserved capacity; Savings via AWS commitments.
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the widest model choice (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Nova) behind one API.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token/character; Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) for provisioned throughput (e.g., ~25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained); committed-use discounts.
key_features: Grounding with Google Search / RAG Engine
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud shops and teams wanting Gemini plus strong multimodal (Imagen/Veo) and a large open-model garden.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits; LLM functions billed per token/credit consumed within the warehouse.
key_features: Models run inside Snowflake governance boundary
No data movement out of Snowflake
platforms.best_for: Organizations with data already in Snowflake wanting AI directly on governed data without ETL or data egress.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for Foundation Model APIs, pay-per-token or provisioned throughput endpoints.
platforms.best_for: Lakehouse-centric enterprises combining custom model training, RAG, and governed data on Databricks.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) token-based consumption; SaaS, hybrid, and on-prem/Cloud Pak deployment options.
key_features: Named Gartner Leader for DSML Platforms 2026
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and hybrid/on-prem deployments prioritizing AI governance, risk, and explainability.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for provisioned/isolated capacity.
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and Fusion application customers wanting GenAI with dedicated capacity and data sovereignty.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: Various open embedding / image / speech models
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-neuron / per-request usage; generous free tier and low per-unit serverless pricing.
platforms.best_for: Latency-sensitive, globally distributed apps needing cheap serverless open-model inference at the edge.

platforms.name: NVIDIA NIM / AI Enterprise
compliance: Runs within customer-controlled infra for GDPR/HIPAA alignment
platforms.pricing: Per-GPU licensing under NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription; deploy on any cloud or on-prem.
key_features: Runs in customer VPC / on-prem / air-gapped
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting fully self-hosted, portable, GPU-optimized model serving with maximum data control.
